questions.prompt: Describe the association between hours of sleep and reaction time in the data (5, 320), (6, 300), (6.5, 290), (7, 280), (8, 260), (9, 255): its direction, form, and strength.
questions.prompt_markup: Describe the association between hours of sleep and reaction time in the data (5, 320), (6, 300), (6.5, 290), (7, 280), (8, 260), (9, 255): its direction, form, and strength.
questions.correct_answer: Negative, roughly linear, and strong: more sleep goes with shorter reaction times.

questions.response: draw on the figure and write an answer
questions.prompt: Make a scatter plot of years since 2000 (x) and phones in millions (y): (0, 1), (2, 1.5), (4, 2.3), (6, 3.4), (8, 5.1), (10, 7.6) Which type of model does the plot suggest?
questions.prompt_markup:
Make a scatter plot of years since 2000 (x) and phones in millions (y):
(0, 1), (2, 1.5), (4, 2.3), (6, 3.4), (8, 5.1), (10, 7.6)
Which type of model does the plot suggest?
questions.correct_answer: Exponential: the points curve upward, growing by about 1.5 times every 2 years.
questions.drawing_answer: Six points rising from left to right and curving upward
questions.grading_note: Form required: the model type with a reason. Both the plot and the answer are graded.

questions.skill: Choose an exponential model from a scatter plot and solve it with logarithms
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A model for the phone data is y = 1(1.22)^x, where x is years since 2000 and y is millions of phones. When does it predict 20 million? Round to the nearest tenth. (log means base 10.)
questions.prompt_markup: A model for the phone data is y = 1(1.22)^x, where x is years since 2000 and y is millions of phones. When does it predict 20 million? Round to the nearest tenth. (log means base 10.)
questions.grading_note: Form required: rounded to the nearest tenth. x = log 20 ÷ log 1.22 ≈ 15.07.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Evaluate claims based on scatter plots
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A website plots shoe size against reading score for students in Grades 1 to 8, finds a strong positive association, and claims that bigger feet improve reading. What is wrong?
questions.prompt_markup: A website plots shoe size against reading score for students in Grades 1 to 8, finds a strong positive association, and claims that bigger feet improve reading. What is wrong?
questions.correct_answer: Age (grade) is a lurking variable: older students have bigger feet and read better. Observational data do not show cause.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation.
